_comment: Bible designer, axis 5 of 5 (story/designer/INTERVIEW.md): read the design back in the author's words and settle what the AI always sees. Column names are prompt tokens: the model reads 'Resolve: 4', so the name is the author's word, never a slug. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY.
goal: Confirm every table, column, unit and rule in the author's words, and decide what the AI always knows, fetches when needed, or never repeats.

questions.ask: Here are the tables and columns as I have them, in your words. Anything to rename, merge or drop?
questions.why: The read-back is where a name the designer guessed gets replaced by the author's.
questions.listenFor: renames, merges, 'I never call it that'

questions.ask: What units do the numbers use?
questions.why: A unit stops a number being read on the wrong scale (coins or thousands of coins, soldiers or regiments).

questions.ask: Which one or two things about a person should the AI never forget, even when they only pass through a scene?
questions.why: Those become always-tier columns, sent with every prompt that mentions the row. Everything else is sent only when the row is in the scene, so the budget stays small.
questions.listenFor: a class or rank, an allegiance, a defining limit

questions.ask: Is there anything the AI should know but not keep putting on the page — an appearance detail, a secret, a long reference?
questions.why: Appearance a model over-repeats is hidden from prompts; secrets and long references are fetched only on demand.
questions.listenFor: 'it keeps mentioning her hair', spoilers, long lists

questions.ask: Ready for me to make these tables? You can rename, hide or add any column later in the grid.
questions.why: Nothing is applied without the author's OK, and the grid is theirs afterwards.
questions.listenFor: yes / not yet / change one thing first

doneWhen: The author has seen every name in their words, chosen what the AI always sees, and said yes to applying.
